question: How would you describe Redis in a backend architecture?
options: A web server for static files
An in-memory data structure store used for caches, counters and short-lived data
A relational database stored in SQL files
A Java compiler
explanation: Redis keeps data in memory and offers simple structures with optional expiry, which suits fast reads, counters and temporary state.

question: Which Spring Boot 4 starter integrates an application with Redis?
options: spring-boot-starter-data-redis
spring-boot-starter-web
spring-boot-starter-jdbc
spring-boot-starter-redis-cache
explanation: spring-boot-starter-data-redis brings Spring Data Redis and the Lettuce driver and auto-configures the connection factory.

question: Why avoid the default JDK serialization for stored objects?
options: Redis rejects those bytes
Spring Boot 4 forbids it
It deletes keys every five minutes
It produces opaque Java-only bytes tied to the class layout
explanation: JDK serialization ties data to a Java class and breaks when the class changes. JSON is readable, smaller and usable from other tools.

question: What distinguishes StringRedisTemplate from RedisTemplate<K, V>?
options: It only works with SQL databases
It cannot set expiry
It is preconfigured for String keys and values
It is read-only
explanation: StringRedisTemplate fixes the serializers to strings, so it needs no configuration for plain text, counters and flags.

question: Which command does increment() on opsForValue() use, and why does it matter?
options: A plain GET followed by SET
The atomic INCR, so concurrent requests never lose a count
A full table lock
A Lua script written by the user
explanation: INCR is atomic on the server, so two clients incrementing at the same time both count. Read-modify-write in the application would lose updates.

question: What should you remember when you store data only in Redis?
options: It lives in memory, so plan for losing it and keep the truth in the database
It is always durable and shared safely
It cannot be expired
It is encrypted by default
explanation: Redis is fast but memory-bound and not the system of record. Keep rebuildable copies there and the authoritative data in the database.
